prior_summary: Transport the object rather than the TCP: a learned attachment-confidence gate exposes causal TCP-to-object rigid transforms to a shared object-token encoder, while both object-to-pad errors remain visible after placement. A learned action-conditioned future-pose predictor supplies masked held-object transform losses to the epsilon diffusion model.
applicable_conditions: State-based Panda parallel-gripper unstack_sort, world poses in metres and wxyz, original absolute joint-position commands. Supports the entire expanded slice: aligned open final approach, closure and lift, attached transport and descent, release and empty retreat, red-to-blue return/approach, and final blue settling. Two causal observations, qpos/qvel, both block poses and both goals are required. The fixed forward interface has no invocation tags: persistent red/blue tokens and red-to-blue/blue-to-none relations replace explicit selected/next tags; arbitrary external role assignments are not supported.
termination_guidance: Continue through closure, descent, release and retreat when a useful physical handoff is needed; a pad predicate can hold while the fingers remain closed. Red exit support includes an open empty gripper returning toward blue with nonzero arm velocity and TCP z about 0.055-0.222 m. Blue exit support includes an open retreat toward TCP z about 0.300 m and final settling. Transfer inside the trained overlap can occur sooner if the successor receives the current state and causal motion evidence. Task completion itself is only red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal under the supplied rotated XY containment and z tolerance, with no required release, clearance, speed or hold condition.
limitations: No force sensing, contact truth, IK, robot FK, image encoder, scripted controller or replay. The attachment gate is a conservative two-frame motion-evidence estimator; it can turn off for stationary held objects and cannot remember attachment across a pause. Explicit selected/next invocation tags are unavailable. Grasp offsets and rotations vary little in training, and arbitrary role order, significant slip, skew grasps, unseen pad directions and recovery are unvalidated. Rotation matrices remove quaternion sign ambiguity but absolute Panda joint actions are not SE(3)-equivariant. Auxiliary future dynamics are learned, not guaranteed constraints.

config.representation: Two persistent color tokens with shared MLP weights, fixed red-to-blue and blue-to-none relations, causal SE(3) grasp transforms gated by learned confidence and conservative motion eligibility, plus absolute robot configuration branch
config.auxiliary_snr_weight: alpha_bar squared; denominator not renormalized by this weight
config.geometry_normalization: Axiswise maximum of supplied complete-demo TCP/red/blue position half-ranges for world vectors, maximum of that vector for rotated local vectors; no fitted per-skill statistics
config.quaternion_representation: Normalized wxyz converted to rotation matrices everywhere; q and -q give identical inputs
config.tag_adaptation: Both color identities and next relationships persist, with no goal-hit target reassignment, external tag input, time index or mutable invocation latch
config.segmentation: All 24 assigned expanded slices, unchanged; all valid action slots contribute to diffusion loss
